title: What massage chair delivery day actually looks like
description: A 200 to 300 pound massage chair does not arrive the way a normal package does. White glove, threshold, and curbside delivery each hand you a different amount of the unboxing and placement work. What each one actually includes before you pick a shipping option.
alt_text: Diagram of the parts inside a massage chair

title: The warranty clock buyers miss: parts vs labor
description: Parts coverage on a massage chair often runs 3 to 5 years. Labor coverage, the part that pays someone to install the free part, often runs only 1 year. The gap between those two clocks is where a "free" repair quietly stops being free.

title: 5 signs your massage chair is actually a return
description: A massage chair sold as new should arrive in a sealed box with its full accessory kit. A return or RMA sticker, a missing power cable, or scuffed leather are signs a different buyer already sent this exact unit back. What to check before you sign for delivery.
alt_text: Massage chair in a living room

title: Check this before you buy a massage chair brand
description: A brand name on the box does not tell you how the company behaves after your chair breaks. A free check of its Better Business Bureau complaint record tells you a lot more: look at the complaint mix, not just the raw count, and watch for parts shipped before diagnosis or tickets closed for non-response.
